correctness.rationale: A complete all-m proof counts the image boundaries of the two monotonic logistic branches, proves m|4j² iff R_m|j by prime valuations, treats even/odd central cells and boundary contacts explicitly, and proves sharp m/R_m<=2sqrt(m). Ergodicity follows from x=sin²(pi t) and doubling. The standalone checker independently enumerates all positive-measure ordered bin pairs by exact integer interval comparisons for 511 resolutions and 100 sharp examples; those finite checks are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Under the material inspected, no exact all-resolution prime-divisibility logistic graph edge-census theorem covers this claim. The 2007 directly related network construction gives an approximate three-edge mean and an endpoint-inclusive four-bin example, not the positive-measure count 3m-m/R-(m mod 2), its sharp 2sqrt(m) arithmetic correction, or typical-orbit realization. The 2026 paper abstract and deposited code compute empirical networks without stating the exact number-theoretic census; the full 2026 paper body was inaccessible, a material residual priority risk. Multiple semantic record queries and accessible own claims were compared by mathematical implication, not title.
residual_risks: Complete main preprint arXiv:2608.20956 text was inaccessible; its uninspected pages could contain a closer result.
Further older literature could encode the same all-resolution edge count under a Ulam matrix, topological transition matrix or graph-degree terminology.
Specific endpoint-inclusive graph constructions in 2007 are not numerically identical to the positive-measure support convention, and finite simulated trajectories need not exhibit all support edges.

value.rationale: The total directed support-edge count is a natural invariant of equal-amplitude state-transition networks used in active logistic-map research. Its prime-power formula sharpens the old approximate mean-degree-three observation to an all-resolution arithmetic law, proves a nontrivial sharp sqrt(m) deficit family rather than an arbitrary numeric tweak, and links the ideal graph to almost-sure long-trajectory observations. This is an exact motivated structural baseline, not merely re-enumeration of one known fixed-size matrix.
